source_text:
∆ιάνοιά ἐστι δύναμις τῆς ψυχῆς, καθ' ἣν μετὰ
συλλογισμοῦ δύναται γινώσκειν τὰ πράγματα· διὸ καὶ λέγεται διάνοια, παρὰ τὸ ὁδόν

τινα διανοίγειν. ∆όξα ἐστὶ δύναμις τῆς ψυχῆς, καθ' ἣν ἄνευ αἰτίας γινώσκει τὸ
πράγματα. Φαντασία δύναμίς ἐστι τῆς ἀλόγου ψυχῆς. Αἴσθησίς ἐστι δύναμις τῆς ψυχῆς,
ἀντιληπτικὴ τῶν ὑλῶν.
thought_title: Definitions of the soul's remaining powers
orientation: John of Damascus is defining the five powers of the soul one by one, having just defined the intellect and now defining discursive thought, opinion, imagination, and sense perception.
pass_a_gloss: Discursive thought is a power of the soul, according to which with syllogism it is able to know the matters; therefore also it is called discursive thought, from opening a certain way. Opinion is a power of the soul, according to which without cause it knows the matters. Imagination is a power of the non-rational soul. Sense perception is a power of the soul, capable of apprehending material things.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the power of knowing through reasoning.
Fixed glossary term for the power of knowing without cause or demonstration.
Fixed glossary term for the power of the non-rational soul.
Fixed glossary term for the soul's power of apprehending material things.
Renders the adjective with its genitive object literally; 'apprehending' captures the grasping sense of ἀντιληπτική.
Literal rendering of the etymological explanation; preserves the wordplay on διάνοια and διανοίγειν.
rejected: from the opening of a path

pass_b_english: Discursive thought is a power of the soul by which it can know matters through a syllogism. It is called discursive thought because it opens a certain way. Opinion is a power of the soul by which it knows matters without a cause. Imagination is a power of the non-rational soul. Sense perception is a power of the soul capable of apprehending material things.
